title: Design of Novel Analog Compute Paradigms with Ark
problem: Existing analog circuit design methodologies are either highly specialized to conventional circuits like filters and ADCs, or implement highly reconfigurable but resource-inefficient accelerators. There is a need for specialized reconfigurable circuits in the intermediate design space with appropriate co-design methodologies.
motivation: Analog computing offers efficiency potential, and systematic design tools and methodologies are needed to enable exploration of this intermediate design space for practical analog compute systems.
method: Ark is a programming language for describing analog compute paradigms that enables progressive incorporation of analog behaviors into computations. It includes a validator for verification and a dynamical system compiler for simulation, allowing systematic evaluation of design trade-offs and non-idealities across different analog computation implementations.
key_novelty: Ark is a programming language that systematically enables design exploration and non-ideality evaluation for specialized reconfigurable analog compute circuits through a validator and dynamical system compiler.
contributions: Ark programming language for describing and designing analog compute paradigms
Validator and dynamical system compiler for verification and simulation of analog computations
Methodology for exploring design trade-offs in reconfigurable analog circuits
Case studies demonstrating design space exploration for three exemplary analog circuit problems
primary_theme: Programming language for analog compute circuit design
